interactionPlan.concept: The Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) of a box filter is a periodic, discrete sinc function (Dirichlet kernel) whose main lobe width is inversely proportional to the spatial width of the box.
learningObjectives: Identify how the peak amplitude of the discrete sinc function at zero frequency equals the sum of the spatial filter coefficients (2L + 1)
Explain the inverse relationship between the spatial width of the box filter (L) and the spectral width of the main lobe
Describe how the periodicity of the DFT (N) determines the spacing between identical spectral copies
interactionPlan.keyInsight: A wider spatial box filter concentrates more energy into a narrower frequency band (low-pass filter effect), raising the peak height while squeezing the lobes closer together.

interactions.label: Box Half-Width (L)
interactions.effect: Modulates the number of non-zero elements in the spatial box filter. In the plot, increasing L increases the main peak's height (to 2L + 1) and narrows the main frequency lobe, creating more zero-crossings (side lobes).
interactions.teaches: The inverse frequency-scaling property: wider spatial filters result in narrower frequency responses.

interactions.label: DFT Size (N)
interactions.effect: Controls the period of the DFT. Adjusting this shifts the locations of the secondary periodic peaks (which occur at multiples of N) closer together or further apart along the u-axis.
interactions.teaches: How discrete sampling in the spatial domain leads to periodic replication in the frequency domain, with a period of exactly N.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: A discrete stem plot showing Box_L[u] values on the y-axis against frequency index u on the x-axis. Stems are blue lines with circular markers at the top. The plot should display at least one full period on both sides of the origin (from approximately -N to N). Highlight key annotations including the main peak value at u=0 (annotated as 2L + 1) and the periodic replications at u = -N and u = N.
